title: Normalized classical Weil restriction on one finite-field model
statement: For the finite-field datum D, l and Ω, any supplied normalized realization R, completed system S, scalar-realization family A and RestrictionComparison C [def-zl-classical-lisse-restriction-models; def-zl-classical-lisse-restriction-maps], let Y₀ be separated and finite type over the original finite field. Let M be a common-stage heart object on its geometric fibre, P a supplied partition with its chosen lattices, and K an ambient Weil complex with carrier exactly M.obj. Fix m≥1 and an actual RestrictionModel V defined over the mth finite extension and factoring through a stratum [def-zl-classical-frontier-restriction-data]. Suppose its support map is the canonical base-change geometric map and supply the resulting Frobenius commutation square. Then there exists a WeilRestrictionResult for these exact data: the classical lift realizes the ambient mth Weil iterate and inverse, the pair and its two equations occur at one finite coefficient enlargement, and a finite sf Weil model has the prescribed normalized fibre comparisons intertwining every actual local Frobenius iterate. No frontier or Frobenius-stable original lattice is assumed.

source.place: Paragraphs 6-7; normalized classical restriction, descent of the finite frontier and its actual Weil structures.

proof.text:
Now assume $T=Y$, let $\theta:Lg_Y^*M\xrightarrow{\sim}M$ be the Weil structure of [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex], and fix the stated $m,j_0,j$. Write $F_f=Lf^*$ and use the normalized composition map $c_{a,b}:F_{ba}\xrightarrow{\sim}F_aF_b$. Put $g=g_Y^m$ and $h=g_V$. Since $j_0$ is defined over $k_m$, $gj=jh$: on base-change coordinates both compositions apply $\gamma^m$ only to the $k$-coordinate. Here $\gamma^m$ is the inverse of $z\mapsto z^{q^m}$, so it fixes $k_m$ pointwise; the Frobenius is geometric, not the absolute Frobenius of $Y$. Form
$$C_j=c_{h,j}\,c_{j,g}^{-1}:F_jF_gM\xrightarrow{\sim}F_hF_jM.$$
The equality of scheme morphisms identifies the two middle composite-pullback objects. Using the iterated Weil map of the local-Frobenius definition, define
$$\alpha_j=F_j(\theta^{[m]})C_j^{-1}:F_hF_jM\xrightarrow{\sim}F_jM.$$
Its inverse is $C_jF_j((\theta^{[m]})^{-1})$. Functoriality and the two inverse equations for $\theta^{[m]}$ prove both inverse equations for $\alpha_j$. The completed comparison theorem supplies exactly these $c$'s, including their equality-of-morphisms, associativity and finite-scalar compatibilities. This construction uses the actual ambient map even when $M$ is not globally lisse; no realization comparison on a nonexistent global classical lisse model is used.

source.place: Paragraph 7: restriction of the original Weil structure; explicit normalized completed-pullback formula

proof.text: Let $L$ be the classical rational system restricted to $V$ in Step 1, and let $\mathcal R$ be normalized classical realization. Its specified isomorphism $\rho:\mathcal R L\xrightarrow{\sim}F_jM$ is already supplied by Step 1. The lisse comparisons identify $\mathcal R(h^*L)$ with $F_h\mathcal R L$: this uses ordinary system pullback, inverse limit and raw rationalization, followed by the normalized lisse scalar realization. The lisse comparison applies to $h$ although $h$ is not $k$-linear. Conjugating $\alpha_j$ by these comparisons gives an arrow $A:\mathcal R(h^*L)\to\mathcal R L$ and its inverse $B$. Fullness gives rational classical maps $u:h^*L\to L$ and $v:L\to h^*L$ realizing $A,B$. Faithfulness gives $uv=1_L$ and $vu=1_{h^*L}$, since realization sends the two composites to $AB=1$ and $BA=1$. Consequently $u$ is the required classical rational Weil isomorphism, its inverse is $v$, and both realize the actual restrictions from Step 2. Only rational maps were lifted; neither map is asserted to preserve the chosen lattice.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.4(1),(4), Proposition 6.8.14(2); fullness and faithfulness applied after the normalized pullback comparisons

proof.text: The classical $\Omega$-Hom groups are the directed colimits in the definition of lisse algebraic-coefficient sheaves. Choose finite stages representing $u$ and $v$, take their compositum with the given $E$, then enlarge to stages witnessing $uv=1$ and $vu=1$. Taking one more compositum makes both equations hold at once. This is finite because there are only two maps and two equations; all objects are the base extensions of the original lattice and its pullback. The sf Hom groups have the same equality-after-enlargement convention, so if representatives of the realization identifications are needed, include their finitely many maps and equalities in this same choice. Thus the map, inverse and equations are represented at one common finite coefficient enlargement, with the normalized scalar comparisons. For the finitely many frontier pieces below, the compositum of these choices works simultaneously. No integral Frobenius invariance has been deduced or used.

source.place: Paragraph 7: the restriction is rational; finite common-stage Hom-colimit assembly

proof.text: For a geometric point $x:s=\operatorname{Spec}k\to V$, the normalized classical-system comparison identifies its classical adic fibre with the sf fibre, including point transport for every automorphism of $s$ and its iterates. The lisse realization also identifies pullback on maps and its composition maps. For each $r\geq1$ the iterate of $\alpha_j$ equals $F_j(\theta^{[mr]})C_{j,r}^{-1}$, where $C_{j,r}:F_jF_{g_Y^{mr}}M\to F_{h^r}F_jM$ is defined as in Step 2. Indeed this is Step 2 for $r=1$; multiplying by $F_{h^r}(\alpha_j)$, naturality moves $F_j\theta^{[m]}$ past the comparison and associativity combines the comparisons into $C_{j,r+1}$. The recursion for $\theta^{[n]}$ gives the formula for $r+1$. If $x$ lies over $\mathbf F_{q^{mr}}$, then $h^rx=xg_s^{mr}$. The local operator is, by definition, the point transport $I^{[mr]}$, followed by the comparison for this return, followed by pullback of $\alpha_j^{[r]}$. Each of these three factors agrees in the classical and sf models: respectively by point-transport compatibility, by normalized composition coherence, and by the realized map in Step 3 and the iterate formula. Their composites therefore agree. This proves the assertion for every local geometric-Frobenius iterate, including iterates at closed points.
